task: Allow the trusted Release Unit Execution workflow to dispatch exact child CI proof runs without widening untrusted workflow authority.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal replay on trusted Release Unit Execution #152 (run 37615831101) successfully materialized the fresh U01 superseding branch and created the bot child PR, but exact child proof dispatch failed with RELEASE_UNIT_CHILD_CI_DISPATCH_FAILED because GitHub returned HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration when gh workflow run ci.yml attempted workflow_dispatch. The trusted executor workflow currently declares actions: read at both workflow and execute-job level, which is insufficient to create a workflow dispatch event.
observableOutcomes: The trusted default-branch Release Unit Execution job can dispatch the exact child CI workflow run after bot PR creation.
The source CI workflow remains read-only and cannot gain write authority.
Only the trusted executor job receives the minimum GitHub Actions permission required for workflow dispatch.
The existing exact PR/head/base/branch identity validation and child-proof import remain unchanged and fail closed.
The unchanged U01 rehearsal proceeds beyond RELEASE_UNIT_CHILD_CI_DISPATCH_FAILED without manual approval, PAT, receipt edit or alternate proof path.
unresolvedRisks: Granting actions: write too broadly could allow unrelated workflow mutation or dispatch from an untrusted execution context.
Changing repository-wide/default permissions would violate least privilege and expand authority beyond the trusted executor.
A dispatch permission fix without exact-head identity checks could prove the wrong child commit.
Using a PAT or user token would bypass the canonical GitHub Actions authority model and create unmanaged credentials.

in: Raise GitHub Actions permission from read to write only where the trusted Release Unit Execution job needs workflow_dispatch.
Preserve contents: write and pull-requests: write exactly as currently required by materialization and merge.
Keep source CI contents read-only and preserve explicit bot child proof dispatch.
Add regression coverage that the trusted executor has actions: write while source CI retains read-only authority.
Replay the immutable rehearsal source after exact-head proof and merge.
out: No PAT, fine-grained token, GitHub App token or manual workflow dispatch workaround.
No change to child proof identity matching, release-state receipts, material operations or risk thresholds.
No Template Factory, Builder, storefront, database, auth, payment or inventory work.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This permission controls whether the trusted release executor may trigger CI proof for code it just materialized. Too little permission deadlocks the release path; too much permission widens automation authority. Least-privilege and exact-context proof are therefore required.

acceptanceCriteria: Release Unit Execution can invoke gh workflow run ci.yml using the repository GITHUB_TOKEN without HTTP 403.
The execute job declares actions: write and no broader workflow gains Actions write authority.
CI continues to expose only read permissions for source-side execution and child proof remains exact-head bound.
Regression proof asserts both the positive executor permission and the negative source-CI permission boundary.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure pass before merge.
After merge, the immutable rehearsal source reaches child proof dispatch and continues beyond the current blocker.
invariants: Only the trusted default-branch executor may receive actions: write.
Source revisions remain data; executor code always comes from main.
Child proof dispatch inputs remain exact PR/head/base/branch identities.
No manual approval or alternate proof artifact may substitute for canonical child CI.
No additional repository permission is granted beyond the minimum required action.

failureModes: Executor retains actions: read and dispatch continues to fail 403.
actions: write is granted at repository/workflow scope more broadly than needed.
Source CI receives write permission and untrusted branch code can dispatch workflows.
Exact child identity inputs are omitted or altered while changing permissions.
A credential workaround replaces canonical GITHUB_TOKEN authority.
edgeCases: Bot-created PR pull_request CI is action_required but explicit workflow_dispatch is allowed.
Child proof workflow already exists and exact reusable run is found, so no dispatch is needed.
Dispatch is attempted for an exact same-repository child head.
Dispatch target branch or head differs and existing validation must reject it.
Executor retry occurs after an interrupted dispatch attempt.
Source workflow executes from an untrusted release-execution/source branch and must remain unable to dispatch.

alternatives.summary: Grant actions: write only to the trusted execute job that performs workflow_dispatch.
alternatives.reason: Minimum permission change at the exact authority boundary that performs dispatch.

alternatives.summary: Grant actions: write to the entire Release Unit Execution workflow.
alternatives.reason: Broader than necessary because only execute needs the capability.

alternatives.summary: Use a PAT or other user credential for workflow dispatch.
alternatives.reason: Creates unmanaged credential authority and bypasses the repository GITHUB_TOKEN trust model.

alternatives.summary: Require a human to manually start child proof.
alternatives.reason: Breaks resumability, automation and no-manual-bypass requirements.

specialistReviews.finding: Actions write can be dangerous if granted to source-controlled or broad workflow contexts.
specialistReviews.resolution: Grant actions: write only on the trusted default-branch execute job; keep source CI and other jobs read-only.

specialistReviews.finding: The current runtime already dispatches exact child proof; the 403 is purely missing token permission.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve runtime identity logic and repair only the workflow permission envelope.

specialistReviews.finding: Dispatch authority belongs to the trusted executor, not the source workflow.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep main checkout/executor trust boundary unchanged and modify only the executor job permission.

specialistReviews.finding: Run #152 is a deterministic production-like reproduction of the permission failure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add regression asserting actions: write at executor job and actions: read/no-write for CI.

challenge.scenario: The trusted executor creates a child PR and needs to dispatch CI proof.
challenge.finding: actions: read cannot create workflow_dispatch and GitHub returns 403.
challenge.resolution: Grant actions: write on execute job.

challenge.scenario: An untrusted source branch runs source CI.
challenge.finding: If source CI had actions: write, branch-controlled code could gain workflow-dispatch authority.
challenge.resolution: Keep source CI permissions read-only and regression-test the negative boundary.

challenge.scenario: The exact child proof run already exists after an interrupted executor attempt.
challenge.finding: A second dispatch is unnecessary and could duplicate proof runs.

challenge.scenario: A wrong child head/base/branch is supplied to dispatch.
challenge.finding: Permission repair must not relax identity validation.
challenge.resolution: Do not change release-unit-ci-context or runtime identity checks; prove existing exact matching remains referenced.

challenge.scenario: A maintainer suggests repository-wide Actions write or PAT as a shortcut.
challenge.finding: Both widen authority beyond the requirement.
challenge.resolution: Reject both; job-local GITHUB_TOKEN permission is the only selected path.

challenge.scenario: workflow-level permissions remain actions: read while job-level execute requests actions: write.
challenge.finding: GitHub job-level permissions are the effective token permissions for the job and may override workflow defaults; this is the narrowest authority boundary.
challenge.resolution: Set actions: write only under jobs.execute.permissions and retain workflow default actions: read.

challenge.scenario: The executor receives actions: write, but only after a child PR already has a terminal action_required pull_request run.
challenge.finding: The permission fix must not treat the old action_required pull_request run as success or proof; it must dispatch or reuse an exact trusted workflow_dispatch run and keep terminal non-success fail-closed.
challenge.resolution: Preserve current classifyExactChildCiRuns and ensureExactChildProofDispatch semantics; the permission change only enables the trusted dispatch call.

challenge.scenario: The trusted executor is retried after workflow_dispatch succeeded remotely but the executor failed before persisting the resulting child-proof state.
challenge.finding: A retry with actions: write must not blindly create duplicate proof runs or expand authority because of the previous partial execution.
challenge.resolution: Keep reuse-first lookup of exact workflow_dispatch runs by child head and branch before issuing a new dispatch, and regression-prove no permission change alters that idempotency path.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Change only the execute job Actions permission from read to write in release-unit-execution.yml.
Add production-surface regression that executor job has actions: write and CI/source paths do not.
Require exact-head Knowledge/Plan/Edit-Time/Incremental Replay/Release Risk/full tests/typecheck/build/Completion Truth/Lifecycle PASS.
Merge only on exact-head proof, then replay the same immutable rehearsal source and follow U01 child proof dispatch.

requirements.requirement: Trusted release execution must be able to dispatch exact child CI proof while untrusted/source CI retains no Actions write authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Source CI may not gain Actions write authority.
Permission repair may not weaken exact child proof identity binding.

requirements.requirement: The permission change must preserve trusted default-branch execution, exact current main authority and canonical Release Risk.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Actions write may not be granted outside the trusted executor job.

notes: Plan-only transaction created from live Release Unit Execution #152 on main ead5039f1711b4b52a1394bac530a9f3ca1ad5be. Exact blocker: RELEASE_UNIT_CHILD_CI_DISPATCH_FAILED with HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration while gh workflow run ci.yml attempted dispatch for U01 child head be5f2b43a2ac35df25120826b83bd50217afb661. Workflow currently has actions: read at workflow and execute-job scope. No permission implementation is authorized until Plan Before Code passes.
